title: Woolton Pie
subtitle: A wartime vegetable pie with an oatmeal pastry crust
excerpt: A baked pie of mixed root vegetables and oats in a light vegetable sauce, topped with an oatmeal-enriched shortcrust. The original wartime recipe uses whatever vegetables are to hand.
sourceNotes: Woolton Pie was created at the Savoy in 1941 by Francatelli for the Ministry of Food; this is a faithful home-kitchen adaptation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The vegetables can be parboiled and cooled a day ahead. Assemble and bake on the day.

content.text: Woolton Pie was designed to feed well with no meat and minimal fat. The oatmeal pastry has a nutty, slightly rough texture that suits the robust root vegetable filling. Use whichever root vegetables you have; the ratios in this recipe are a guide rather than a strict requirement.

Make the pastry: rub the butter into the flour, oats, and salt until the mixture looks like coarse breadcrumbs. Add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water, one at a time, and bring the dough together. Wrap and chill for 20 minutes.

Put the diced potato, carrot, swede, and parsnip into the large saucepan. Cover with the stock and bring to a simmer. Cook for 8 minutes until the vegetables are just tender but still holding their shape. Remove from the heat.
Stir in the onion, oats, and parsley. Season generously with salt and black pepper. The oats will thicken the liquid as it cools.
Heat the oven to 200C. Transfer the filling to a deep 23cm pie dish and leave to cool slightly for 10 minutes.
Roll the oatmeal pastry to roughly the size of the pie dish. Lay it over the filling and press the edges down inside the rim of the dish to seal. Trim off any excess.
Brush the top with beaten egg and cut a small slit in the centre. Bake for 30 minutes until the pastry is firm and golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving. Bring the pie dish to the table and spoon portions straight out.

items.cause: The oats absorb liquid, making the pastry drier than standard shortcrust.
items.fix: Add an extra teaspoon of cold water and press the cracks back together. This pastry is forgiving: patch any splits before baking.

items.symptom: The filling is too liquid under the lid.
items.cause: The oats in the filling did not have time to absorb the stock before baking.
items.fix: Let the filling sit for 10 minutes off the heat before transferring to the dish. If it still looks watery, stir in an extra tablespoon of oats.

items.cause: They were simmered too long before baking.
items.fix: Cook for no more than 8 minutes; they will continue cooking in the oven under the pastry lid.
